purpose: Preserve distinct top/rapid transfer identities when Ribasim owns surface-water storage. Do not collapse hydrologically different SWAP destinations merely because they share the same sign in the Ribasim Basin balance.

legacy_authority.qrapdra: positive rapid/macropore drainage into secondary surface water
legacy_authority.runots_positive: positive soil-surface/runoff amount into secondary surface water
legacy_authority.runots_negative: negative inundation amount from secondary surface water to SWAP top boundary

qrapdra_positive.ribasim_balance_role: positive drainage-class or separately identified inflow
qrapdra_positive.requirement: retain RAPID_DRAINAGE transfer identity outside any aggregate Basin forcing

runots_negative.requirement: must remain distinguishable from lower RIBASIM_TO_SWAP infiltration when both are active

hard_invariants: Negative RUNOTS is not encoded as negative Ribasim surface_runoff.
Lower infiltration and top inundation are distinct interface transfers even if Ribasim may aggregate them in a Basin water balance.
Rapid drainage and ordinary drainage may be aggregated for Basin mass only after their individual accepted transfer identities remain auditable.
A rejected top-boundary candidate may not change accepted Ribasim storage.
Exactly-once mass booking applies independently to each transfer identity.
minimum_future_cases: negative top inundation with sufficient Ribasim storage
simultaneous lower infiltration and top inundation proving destination identity is not lost
availability-limited negative top inundation causing transaction recomposition
design_decision: Prefer explicit coupler transfer records as the scientific authority. Ribasim Basin forcing names are balance endpoints, not ownership labels. If multiple outward transfers share a Ribasim aggregate forcing, the coupler ledger must preserve their split before aggregation.
